newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee untraded, rate near central bank.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee untraded, rate near central bank.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was untraded two hours after opening because the dollar-rupee exchange rate was quoted near the Central Bank's top level, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee was quoted at 57.86 to the dollar, after opening at 57.84, they said. The rupee closed at 57.87 on Friday.
"With the rate so near the Central Bank top, business will go the the Central Bank," said a dealer at Panasia Bank.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by a quarter local cent and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.7245 and 57.8705.
Call money, meanwhile was at 15 percent, after opening at 14.5 percent, dealers said.

While cautioning that call rates could climb if banks continued to buy dollars from the Central Bank, dealers said the Central Bank's intention of taking 500 million rupees worth of Treasury Bills at this week's auction was a good sign.
Banks have been covering imports with dollars from the Central Bank since last Thursday.
"Liquidity will improve by 500 million rupees when the Central Bank takes these Treasury Bills," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
